VitaHarvest Foods - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the VitaHarvest Foods Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A, please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss VitaHarvest Foods' Q3 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Growth Officer; and Taylor Kim, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on five key areas: performance of key brands and product categories, discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies, impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue, capital expenditure plans and priorities, and revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance.

First, regarding performance of key brands and product categories: Good afternoon, everyone—though it's morning here, the momentum feels like midday success. As we review our Q3 outcomes, our key brands and product categories propelled 6.2% organic net sales growth, surpassing the full-year midpoint target of 4-5%. This held firm against easing input cost inflation at 2-3% quarter-over-quarter and shifting consumer preferences toward premium and health-oriented items. Let me outline this by segment, drivers, regions, and the initiatives sustaining our edge.

Our beverage segment, comprising 42% of total net sales, surged 8.1% organically, with volumes rising 4.2% and price/mix adding 3.9%. Leading the charge is our flagship Zest Energy Drinks brand, which achieved 12.5% double-digit growth for the ninth consecutive quarter. This stems from rolling out Zest Zero Ultra, a zero-sugar, electrolyte-enhanced functional drink that grabbed 1.2 share points in the U.S. energy category according to Nielsen, surpassing rivals like Monster and Red Bull. Over in APAC, Zest's ready-to-drink iced teas jumped 15% in volume, capitalizing on premium tea surges similar to Unilever's Lipton and PepsiCo's Pure Leaf.

The hydration lineup, featuring AquaPure still and sparkling waters, posted solid 9.8% growth, bolstered by margin gains from alkaline filtration innovations that trimmed production expenses 7% year-over-year through smarter water sourcing deals. Across beverages, EBITDA margins widened 120 basis points to 28.4%, aided by efficiencies from new aseptic filling operations in Mexico that reduced downtime 18%.

Moving to snacks and confectionery, 35% of sales, organic growth came in at 3.7%, with volumes essentially flat at 0.1% and price/mix contributing 3.6%. Crunchy Bites, our savory snack flagship, advanced 2.1% despite category softness, picking up 0.8 share points in North American convenience stores through air-fried, low-sodium options echoing Kellogg's Pringles clean-label updates. SweetPeak chocolate confectionery encountered a 1.2% setback from 25% year-over-year global cocoa inflation per ICCO figures, but hedging and palm oil swaps contained margin erosion to 50 basis points.

Our health and wellness standout, nutri-snacks including VitaBar protein and fiber bars, rocketed 18.4% organically—volumes plus 11%, price/mix plus 7.4%—tapping the $50 billion global functional foods surge like Mondelez's Clif Bar playbook, with e-commerce now at 22% of sales versus 14% last year.

Dairy and plant-based alternatives, 18% of the mix, advanced 5.9%, spearheaded by PureLact extended-shelf-life milks and the rapidly expanding GreenMoo oat and almond milks, up 22% amid dairy shift trends. In EMEA, GreenMoo snagged 2.1 share points in the UK plant-based milk space per Kantar, pulling ahead of Oatly as almond costs stabilized.

By region, North America at 55% of sales led with 7.4% organic growth, fueled by club giants Costco and Sam's Club supplying 25% of snack volumes in bulk premium formats. EMEA managed 2.8%, countering UK biscuit volume dips with 14% functional beverage gains in Germany and France. APAC exploded 11.2%, powered by Tmall in China where Zest and VitaBar soared over 30%, while LATAM hit 6.5% despite FX turbulence, supported by Mexico's beverage nearshoring.

Driving forces include premiumization contributing 2.8 points to price/mix, as shoppers upgrade to ready-to-drink functionals and low/no-sugar picks—our zero-calorie beverage share now 35%, up from 22% in 2022. Health-focused items outpaced core growth by 3x, matching Nielsen's 7% CAGR forecast for functionals to 2027.

On strategy, our Taste for Tomorrow innovation pipeline delivered 12 new SKUs in Q3, with AI flavor modeling slashing R&D time 30%. Sustainability efforts feature recyclable pouches on 60% of snacks, cutting virgin plastic 15% and securing EcoVadis Platinum plus more retailer slots. Our DTC TasteMasters app has 5 million users, lifting NPS 18% and basket sizes 12%. Supply chain hedges cover 80% of 2024 inputs, with precision ag for cocoa and nuts boosting yields 10%.

Forward, category tailwinds from normalized at-home use and away-from-home rebound set us for 5-7% organic growth in FY24. Brand media up 8% to 12.5% of sales locks in share amid industry fragmentation.

Second, concerning discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies: Turning to our Q3 numbers, net revenues climbed 7.2% year-over-year to $8.3 billion, our eighth straight quarter of organic expansion. Pricing fueled 8.1 percentage points, more than covering a slight 0.9-point volume dip, with mix adding 1.2 points from healthier beverages and snacks, and FX a minor 0.6-point boost.

Our pricing moves averaged 9-11% across core lines, weighted at 9.5%, the most measured since 2022's inflation crest, guided by elasticity models pegging tolerance at -2.1, superior to NielsenIQ's -2.5 category norm. Beverages, 45% of revenue, got mid-single-digit lifts on Zest Cola-style soft drinks and juices, recovering 85% of HFCS and aluminum spikes. Salty snacks took bolder 10-12% rises to shield against PepsiCo's Lay's and Frito-Lay, where private labels bite hardest.

We tailored approaches: Everyday Low Pricing resets on U.S. high-velocity items cut promo depth 150 basis points to 18% of list, while High-Low played in EMEA impulse lines like NutriCrunch bars. Pricing stuck at 92% take rate within 90 days, improved from 85%.

Our Revenue Growth Management framework bolsters pricing with promotion, product, and placement. Trade spend dropped to 22% of revenue, down 200 basis points, redirecting to loyalty app shopper marketing. The Value Pack Plus initiative in the U.S. boosted family packs of PureHarvest yogurt drinks 3% in basket size using IRI insights for top events.

Premium mix thrives: plant-based drinks and functional snacks volumes up 15%, now 28% of beverages from 22% two years back, akin to Nestlé's Garden of Life and Mondelez protein pushes. Innovations like zero-sugar VitalQuench energy waters added 1.5 mix points, grabbing share in the $12 billion RTD hydration arena for Gen Z health seekers.

Regionally, North America (52%) pricing drove 9.8 points amid lingering inflation, offsetting 1.2% at-home volume softness with 1,200 new club SKUs at Costco. EMEA (22%) pricing leaped 12.3 points with 11% Western Europe hikes against dairy/wheat swings from Ukraine issues; volumes steady via 4% premium adult bev growth like Diageo patterns. APAC (18%) balanced at 6.5% organic, pricing 7.2 points plus 1% volumes from e-com; Tmall/Shopee ignited 25% Greater China RTD tea revenue. LATAM closed at 8%, pricing 10 points passing commodity costs despite currencies.

Tech powers it: $150 million in SymphonyAI pricing analytics for ZIP-level elasticity and competitor response via Kroger data. Blockchain for cocoa cuts input swings 15%, enabling Green Deal premiums.

Ahead, pricing eases to 4-6% as sugar futures fall 18%, but RGM targets mid-single-digit organic via pruning low-RGM SKUs (<5% margins) and $2+ innovations to 30% revenue by 2025. Elasticity flags below -2.3 trigger value tweaks sans brand harm.

Our RGM fortifies growth versus peers like Coca-Cola and Unilever.

Third, in terms of impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue: Before segment deep dives, let's address FX's top-line drag this quarter from the robust U.S. dollar. VitaHarvest draws 42% of its $33.5 billion trailing twelve-month revenue internationally: Europe 18%, Latin America 12%, Asia-Pacific 9%. Brands like Zest Cola, Sparkle Waters, NutriCrunch, and TropiFruit depend on local sales converted to USD.

Reported Q3 revenue rose 2.8% to $8.3 billion; constant currency, it's 7.2%—a $280 million FX hit, 65 basis points off growth, akin to Q2's $250 million but better than Q1's $420 million as dollar index topped 105 on Fed hawkishness.

Europe led the drag at 45%, euro down 8.2% on ECB cuts and weak PMI in snacks/confectionery. Local beverage volumes up 4% on Sparkle Waters summer demand in Germany/UK, but reported sales fell 3.1% vs. 5.2% constant; NutriCrunch in France/Italy hit by Aldi/Lidl pricing.

Latin America mixed: Brazil real up 4.5% on Selic hikes gave $35 million tailwind (+0.5%), countering Argentina peso's 12% drop amid 200% inflation. Constant currency LATAM soared 11% on TropiFruit juices, 15-20% pricing sans volume loss, like Coca-Cola FEMSA.

APAC -$60 million from India rupee -6%, yen softness. Constant 9% growth led by Indonesia/Vietnam Zest RTD teas in $15 billion market (8% CAGR, Nielsen); China flat locally worsened to -2% reported.

Dollar index up 11% YTD pressures F&B peers—PepsiCo's 2% organic hid 5% constant, Nestlé 200 bps H1 drag. Our 70% EM exposure sees 15% annualized volatility (IMF). USD inputs like sugar/cocoa mismatch weakening locals.

Mitigations: 75% twelve-month hedges (50% forwards, 25% options), natural hedges sourcing 60% LATAM sugar locally via Copersucar. AI elasticity dynamic pricing in 15 markets recouped 30% Q3 FX.

Q4 FX 50-75 bps drag at DXY 103-106, but 6-8% constant growth shines via health bevs (+12%) and premium snacks (+9%) in FX-free North America (+5%).

Fourth, looking at capital expenditure plans and priorities: As we close out Q3, let's explore our FY2024 and beyond capex plans and priorities. VitaHarvest is in a transformative stage, channeling disciplined capex to become a nimbler, greener, innovation powerhouse in Food & Beverage. I'll cover budget, initiatives, regions, and strategic alignment.

FY2024 capex guides to $1.4 billion, 12% above FY2023's $1.25 billion, or 4.2% of $33.5 billion projected sales—matching PepsiCo and Mondelez at 4-5% amid inflation and supply shifts. ROIC targets 12-14%, 3-4 year paybacks, backed by 95% free cash flow to adjusted EBITDA.

Capex splits into four pillars for resilience, premiumization, sustainability:

Manufacturing expansion takes 45% or $630 million, targeting plant-based, ready-meals, functionals (8-10% global CAGR, Nielsen). Highlights: $250 million greenfield in Querétaro, Mexico for VitaPlant oat/almond drinks—30% less water via recycling, adding 20% Americas capacity for $15B U.S. non-dairy. $150 million Georgia snack upgrades with Tetra Pak aseptic for HarvestCrunch bars vs. KIND/RXBAR, +25% throughput, -15% labor.

Supply chain resilience 25% or $350 million post-Red Sea/pandemic: $120 million three automated DCs—Shanghai APAC, Rotterdam Europe, São Paulo LATAM—with KION robotics cutting errors 40%, same-day Amazon Fresh. $100 million controlled storage for salad inputs vs. droughts like Dole's lettuce woes, de-risking 250 bps COGS freight inflation.

Sustainability/ESG 20% or $280 million to 2035 net-zero Scope 1&2: $180 million energy upgrades—biomass/solar at 12 plants, -25% GHG; Wisconsin dairy digesters -18% costs like Nestlé. $100 million recyclable packaging for bev multipacks, ISCC rPET -40% virgin plastic for Gen Z/EU directives.

Digital/innovation 10% or $140 million: $80 million SAP S/4HANA to 80% ops by Q4 2025 + Siemens AI maintenance -30% downtime like Unilever. $60 million Palo Alto R&D for precision fermentation probiotics vs. Perfect Day, -20% culturing costs.

Regions: North America 50% ($700M) premium snacks/bevs for $100B healthy snacking, U.S. inflation 2-3%. Europe 20% ($280M) sustainability vs. UK tax, +150 bps EMEA margins. APAC 20% ($280M) China/India RTD teas 12% CAGR. LATAM/ROW 10% ($140M) export hedges vs. BRL/ARS.

Tied to pillars: health/wellness to 15% sales by 2026 (+5 pts), 100 bps annual gross margin gains, resilience vs. cocoa +50%/wheat spikes. Organic funding keeps capex/sales 4%, A- rating, 2.5x debt/EBITDA.

This $1.4B drives 5-7% organic CAGR to 2027, 50 bps ROIC lift, F&B sustainability lead. Q3 on track.

Finally, reviewing revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance: Good morning, and thanks for dialing in. Before closing prepared remarks, an update on FY2024 guidance: we're reaffirming across metrics, underscoring our portfolio diversity, pricing rigor, and Core+Growth framework amid cocoa +150% YTD, inflation fatigue in at-home channels.

Original February guide holds:

Consolidated net revenues $33.0 billion to $33.8 billion, 4-5.5% organic—2 pts pricing, -1 pt volume in mass.

Adjusted diluted EPS $4.80 to $4.95, 6-9% midpoint growth incl. $0.15 VitaPure dilution.

Adjusted EBITDA margin 18.2-18.7%, +40 bps midpoint from productivity vs. inflation.

Free cash flow $1.4-$1.5 billion for $0.80 dividend, $500M repurchases.

Capex $1.4 billion on high-ROI like Mexico aseptic, AI forecasting.

Q3 organic 5.2% beat: Beverages +7.1% (HydroBoost, RTD coffee +22%, e-com +18%); Snacks +2.8% cocoa-hit like Hershey/Mondelez, but 6.5% pricing, premium 32% sales (+4 pts).

Q4 organic 5-6% on holidays, NutriFlex pea-protein snacks for $15B alt-protein (12% CAGR). Conservative 3% USD FX vs. MXN/BRL.

Regions: NA (72%) 4.5% on away-from-home +9%, club, low-sugar vs. FDA labels.

LATAM (15%) 8-10% Mexico ramp, Brazil RTD teas >Ambev.

Europe/APAC (13%) 3%, EU PPWR/China offset by Alibaba JV +25%.

Bottom-line: 5-6% input inflation (Q3 7% down), 70% 2025 cocoa hedged $8,200/MT, dairy mid-single. Q3 gross +120 bps to 38.5% via Project Horizon SAP/ML—working capital -8 to 42 days, shrinkage -15%. SG&A 22.5%, ZBB $80M YTD savings.

Core+Growth: prune 9% low-margin (private nuts), $400M adjacencies functionals/upcycled like Celsius/Beyond. M&A opportunistic; post-VitaPure, debt/EBITDA 2.1x for bolt-ons non-alc.

Reaffirmation signals execution confidence for mid-single growth, 20%+ ROIC.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Maria Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Maria Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Alex. As Alex highlighted, we achieved solid results in Q3 2024. Net sales were $8.3 billion, representing a 6.2% increase year-over-year on an organic basis. Gross margin was 38.5%, impacted by moderating input costs but offset by productivity gains and supply chain efficiencies. Operating income was $1.18 billion, and earnings per share were $1.12. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $2.8 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for net revenues of $33.0 to $33.8 billion, adjusted EPS of $4.80 to $4.95, and other metrics as outlined by Alex.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, thank you. Our first question comes from Mike Thompson with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Mike Thompson (JPMorgan):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Good morning, Mike. Inflation remains a challenge, particularly in commodities like cocoa and dairy, but we've navigated it effectively through our targeted pricing actions averaging 9.5% this quarter, as I detailed earlier, combined with hedging 70% of key inputs and productivity from Project Horizon, which delivered 120 basis points of gross margin expansion. Volumes held resilient in premium categories, and we're seeing input costs ease to 5-6% for the year, positioning us well.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Lisa Chen (Morgan Stanley):
What are your plans for plant-based beverages and what is the expected revenue impact?

Jordan Lee (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Lisa. Our plant-based portfolio, including VitaPlant oat milk and GreenMoo almond lines, is a cornerstone of our health and wellness push. The new Querétaro facility ramps capacity 20% for the Americas, targeting the $15 billion U.S. non-dairy market with 30% lower water use. Early pilots show 15% volume growth in functionals, and we expect this to contribute 1-2 points to FY25 organic revenue, mirroring Oatly's expansions but with better margins through automation. Distribution gains in club and e-com will accelerate this.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with Barclays. Please proceed.

David Patel (Barclays):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Taylor Kim (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
David, thanks for the question. We've prioritized resilience with $350 million in capex for regional DCs in Shanghai, Rotterdam, and São Paulo, featuring robotics for 40% fewer errors and same-day fulfillment. Vertical integration in controlled storage secures fresh inputs against droughts, and we've regionalized sourcing—60% LATAM sugar locally—to counter Red Sea issues and freight inflation. These moves cut working capital days and kept COGS stable despite volatility.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Sarah Lee with Bank of America. Please proceed.

Sarah Lee (Bank of America):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Maria Chen (CFO):
Sarah, our Q4 outlook aligns with the reaffirmed guidance: 5-6% organic growth from holiday strength, NutriFlex launches, and away-from-home recovery. FX a modest drag, but constant currency momentum in beverages and APAC e-com more than offsets. Margins expand via efficiencies, and we're on track for the full-year metrics, with fortress balance sheet for opportunistic M&A.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in VitaHarvest Foods. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
